domain.title: Domains and DNS
domain.intro: Add these records at your domain provider. Mail on {domain} starts as soon as MX and SPF are correct; DKIM and DMARC keep your mail out of spam folders.
domain.mail_ready: MX and SPF are correct. Mail on your domain is active.
domain.mail_not_ready: MX or SPF is not correct yet. DNS changes can take up to a few hours to appear.
domain.purpose_spf: Allows our server to send for your domain
domain.provider: The DNS records of {domain} are managed at {provider}. Sign in there and open the DNS settings of this domain.
domain.provider_unknown: Sign in at the provider that manages the DNS records of {domain} (usually where the domain is registered) and open the DNS settings.
domain.howto_2: Add the records below. Use “Copy” to take name and value exactly. Remove existing MX records; replace an existing SPF record (“v=spf1 …”), because a domain may have only one.
domain.howto_3: Save. Changes usually show up after 15–60 minutes. We check automatically every 15 minutes and email you as soon as everything is right. You can also click “Check DNS” yourself.
domain.name_hint: Some providers expect only the part before your domain as the name (e.g. “_dmarc” instead of “_dmarc.{domain}”) or “@” for the domain itself.
domain.other_mail_title: Attention: {domain} receives email at another provider today
domain.other_mail: Email for {domain} currently goes to {mx}. As soon as you switch the MX record, all new email for @{domain} arrives in xenaxio and the mailboxes at your current provider receive nothing anymore. Create all mailboxes you need in xenaxio first. To try things out, use a subdomain such as test.{domain}.
domain.catchall_hint: Mail to addresses that do not exist on {domain} (for example mistyped names or old addresses) goes to the chosen mailbox. Without this setting it is refused, and the sender gets an error message.
domain.catchall_spam: This usually brings more spam: spammers often try made-up addresses.
domain.catchall_auto_off: If the mailbox is disabled or deleted, the setting turns itself off.
domain.delete_confirm: Remove {domain}? This only works when it has no mailboxes and addresses left. Mail to {domain} is refused afterwards.
domain.added: {domain} was added. Now add the DNS records below.
domain.limit_reached: You use all {limit} domains of your plan. Contact us for more.

mcp.title: Connect AI chats
mcp.intro: Connect your AI chat, for example Claude, to xenaxio. Then ask about your email right in the chat, have replies prepared as drafts and plan meetings. The chat cannot send or delete anything.
mcp.disabled: AI features are switched off for your account. Please contact your administrator.
mcp.howto_1: Open Claude (claude.ai, the desktop app or the mobile app) and go to Settings → Connectors.
mcp.howto_2: Choose “Add custom connector”, enter “xenaxio” as the name and paste this address:
mcp.howto_3: Click “Connect”. xenaxio opens: sign in and confirm with “Allow”.
mcp.howto_4: Done. Ask Claude, for example: “Which of today’s emails are important?”
mcp.howto_other: Other AI chats that support connectors (MCP) connect the same way with this address.
mcp.revoke_confirm: Disconnect “{name}”? The chat loses access to your mailbox at once.
mcp.audit_note: Every access is recorded in the log with the connection’s name.
mcp.advanced_intro: For programs that cannot sign in through a browser, such as your own scripts or automations. The token is shown only once.

mcp.chat_note: If your company uses the team chat, the AI chat can also read and search it (only your channels and direct messages). It cannot write there.

mail_apps.title: Mail apps
mail_apps.intro: With these settings you can also use your mailbox in Outlook, Apple Mail, Thunderbird or the mail app on your phone. Your e-mail stays on the xenaxio server; the web and the app show the same mailbox.
mail_apps.domain_pending: Your company's domain is not connected yet. Until then new e-mail does not arrive at xenaxio and sending is blocked – from mail apps too.
mail_apps.password_note: When you change your password in xenaxio, change it in every mail app too.
mail_apps.outgoing_note: Outgoing mail needs a sign-in: the same user name and password as for incoming mail. If the app asks for the authentication method, choose "Normal password".
mail_apps.send_as_intro: You may also send from these addresses. You do not need another account for this: add the address in your mail app as an extra sender address (an “identity” in Thunderbird, a “From” address in Outlook) and pick it in the “From” field when you write.
mail_apps.send_as_note: The sign-in for outgoing mail stays the same: your user name and your xenaxio password. A shared mailbox has no password of its own.
mail_apps.outlook_1: File → Add account. Enter your e-mail address.
mail_apps.outlook_2: Open "Advanced options", tick "Let me set up my account manually" and click "Connect".
mail_apps.outlook_3: Choose "IMAP" and enter the values above for incoming and outgoing mail, each with SSL/TLS encryption.
mail_apps.outlook_4: Click "Next" and enter your xenaxio password.
mail_apps.outlook_new: New Outlook (Windows) and Outlook for Mac
mail_apps.outlook_new_1: Add an account and enter your e-mail address.
mail_apps.outlook_new_2: When asked for the provider or account type: choose "IMAP", not Exchange or Microsoft 365.
mail_apps.outlook_new_3: Enter the values above for incoming and outgoing mail, enter your xenaxio password and continue.
mail_apps.iphone_1: Settings → Apps → Mail → Mail Accounts → Add Account → Other → Add Mail Account (older iOS: Settings → Mail → Accounts).
mail_apps.iphone_2: Enter your name, e-mail address and xenaxio password, then "Next".
mail_apps.iphone_3: Choose "IMAP" at the top. Under "Incoming Mail Server" and "Outgoing Mail Server" enter the server, user name and password from above.
mail_apps.iphone_4: "Next" and "Save". The iPhone turns SSL on by itself.
mail_apps.mac_2: Enter your name, e-mail address and xenaxio password and click "Sign In".
mail_apps.mac_3: If Mail asks for the servers: choose account type "IMAP" and enter the server and user name from above for incoming and outgoing mail.
mail_apps.thunderbird_1: Account setup → E-mail. Enter your name, e-mail address and xenaxio password.
mail_apps.thunderbird_3: Incoming: IMAP, server and port from above, SSL/TLS, Normal password. Outgoing: SMTP, server and port from above, SSL/TLS, Normal password. The user name is your e-mail address in both.

mail_apps.android_2: Choose "Personal (IMAP)" and enter your xenaxio password.

mail_apps.android_4: Outgoing server: server and port from above, SSL/TLS, sign-in required, same details.

mail_apps.shared: Shared mailboxes (e.g. info@) you have access to are under “Shared Folders” in your mail app. The app files replies from their address in your own “Sent” folder.

shared.title: Shared mailboxes
shared.intro: A shared mailbox such as info@ or billing@ belongs to no single person. You decide who may read it and who may also send from its address. Those people see it as a mailbox of its own in their email and under “Shared Folders” in mail apps. Shared mailboxes do not count towards your employees' mailboxes.

shared.name_hint: What recipients and your team see, e.g. “Info Example Ltd”.

shared.access_hint: “Read”: read email, mark it as read, flag it, move it to folders and delete it, but not send from this address. “Read and send”: also reply and write from this address, from mail apps too. Read/unread is shared by everyone.

Delete {email} for good? All email of this shared mailbox is deleted, which cannot be undone. The address becomes free again.

resources.title: Resources
resources.intro: Your team books rooms, vehicles and equipment by inviting them to an event like a person. xenaxio accepts automatically when the time is free and declines when it is already booked or the invitation does not come from your company. Everyone sees when a resource is booked. Managers also see and change its bookings. Resources do not count towards your employees' mailboxes.

resources.name_hint: How it appears when planning, e.g. “Meeting room 1”.
resources.address_hint: Only for invitations, e.g. room-1. Nobody reads mail to this address.

Delete {email} for good? All bookings of this resource are deleted, which cannot be undone.

memory.title: Assistant
memory.intro: This is what the AI assistant remembers about you, for example how to address you, your signature or your deputy. It only remembers what you tell it yourself and approve with "Confirm" – never anything from emails or files. It uses the notes in the chat and in "Reply with AI".
memory.on: The assistant may remember things and uses your notes.
memory.off: Memory is switched off: the assistant uses no notes and proposes no new ones. Saved notes stay until you delete them.
memory.none: No notes yet. Tell the assistant, for example, "Remember: sign my emails with Best, Anna".
memory.delete_all_confirm: Delete all notes? This cannot be undone.
memory.add_hint: One short sentence, at most {max} characters.
memory.full: {max} notes are already saved. Delete older ones to add new ones.
memory.privacy: Notes are stored encrypted in Germany and sent to the AI only when you use the assistant. Your administrator does not see them; the log only shows that notes changed. External AI chats (MCP) do not see them.

schedules.title: Scheduled tasks ({count} of {max} active)
schedules.intro: Tasks the assistant does on its own, once or regularly. The result arrives in a chat of its own in the assistant, by email too if you like. Your company allows one task at most every {every} and at most {max} runs a day in total.
schedules.how: Set up new ones in the assistant, for example: “Summarize my new emails every morning at 8.” They also show in your calendar “AI tasks”.
schedules.paused_no_access: Paused: access to your mailbox had ended. “Resume” renews it.
schedules.paused_ai_off: Paused: the AI assistant was switched off.
schedules.paused_failures: Paused after three failures in a row.
schedules.run_started: Running – the result will appear in the task's chat shortly.
schedules.delete_confirm: Delete “{title}”? The calendar entry goes, the chat stays.
schedules.company_off: Your company has switched scheduled tasks off. Your tasks are paused; you can see and delete them.
schedules.company_no_send: Your company does not allow the assistant to send on its own: it only saves drafts.
schedules.paused_company_off: Paused: your company had switched scheduled tasks off. Resume it once they are allowed again.
schedules.paused_company_limit: Paused: more tasks than your company allows per person. Pause or delete another one, then resume.
schedules.paused_company_interval: Paused: it runs more often than your company allows. Ask the assistant to schedule it less often.

ownmodel.title: Own AI model
ownmodel.intro: How to run a language model on your own hardware – for example a Mac Studio with 64 GB – and connect it to xenaxio. The server stays behind a Cloudflare Tunnel: no open ports, only requests with your access token get through. The commands are for macOS; on Linux it works the same with your distribution's packages.
ownmodel.s1_title: Install Ollama and load the model
ownmodel.s1_text: Ollama serves the model through an OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:11434/v1.
ownmodel.s1_models: The model must be able to call tools (tool calling), or the assistant cannot read emails, events or files. Understanding images is optional. For 64 GB of memory qwen3.6:35b-a3b fits (fast, as only a small part of the model works per word); alternative: gemma4:31b (slower).
ownmodel.s2_text: Ollama runs as a system service: it starts at boot, even with nobody signed in, with the settings for xenaxio – longer context (the assistant sends about 4,000 tokens with its tools, long emails more), the model stays loaded, two requests at a time. First quit the Ollama app and remove it from the login items (or brew services stop ollama), or two Ollamas will want the same port.
ownmodel.s2_mac: On the Mac: more memory for the graphics unit at every start, never sleep, restart after a power cut.
ownmodel.s2_note: Then restart the Mac once without signing in and test from another device through the tunnel (step 4). If ollama ps shows “CPU” instead of “GPU”, the model runs without the graphics unit and is very slow: remove the service (sudo launchctl bootout system/de.xenaxio.ollama), turn on automatic login and use the Ollama app with “Open at login”. The Mac must be on and online while your team uses the assistant; if it goes down, the admins get an e-mail.
ownmodel.s3_text: You need a domain on Cloudflare (the free plan is enough). Replace llm.ihre-firma.de with an address on your domain.
ownmodel.s3_config: Configuration /etc/cloudflared/config.yml (the create command shows the tunnel ID). httpHostHeader is needed: Ollama only accepts requests addressed to localhost.
ownmodel.s3_host: Put the configuration and the credentials file in place, then run cloudflared as a service (it runs without anyone signed in):
ownmodel.s4_text: In the Cloudflare dashboard under Zero Trust: Access → Service Credentials → create a service token and note Client ID and Client Secret. Then Access → Applications → Self-hosted for llm.ihre-firma.de, with a policy of action “Service Auth” and exactly this service token. Without the token Cloudflare refuses every request.
ownmodel.s4_check: Check (without the headers you must get an error page, with them the list of models):
ownmodel.s5_url: Address: {url}, kind: OpenAI-compatible, leave the API key empty
ownmodel.s5_model: Model: qwen3.6:35b-a3b (as ollama list shows it)
ownmodel.s5_headers: Headers: CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret with the values of the service token
ownmodel.s5_switch: “Save and test” – when every point is green, choose “Own model” above. From then on your team's requests go only to your server.
ownmodel.other_text: Any server with an OpenAI-compatible API works: vLLM (…/v1), LM Studio (server mode, …/v1), Azure OpenAI (…openai.azure.com/openai/v1, key as API key) or a provider of your choice. The address must be publicly reachable over https; xenaxio refuses local and internal addresses.
ownmodel.privacy_text: With an own model, email content, events and files the assistant reads go to your server and – passing through – via Cloudflare. Your company is responsible for that server. If it does not answer, the assistant shows an error; xenaxio does not quietly fall back to Mistral.
ownmodel.s2_check: Check: after an answer, ollama ps shows “100% GPU” in the PROCESSOR column.

calendar_links.title: Calendars from Google, Outlook & co.
calendar_links.intro: Subscribe to your calendars from other services and show your xenaxio events there – by a link, both ways. Subscribed calendars are for viewing: make changes where the calendar comes from.
calendar_links.subscribe_intro: Paste a calendar's iCal address. xenaxio fetches it right away and then every 30 minutes.
calendar_links.name: Name
calendar_links.how_google: Google: open the calendar → Settings and sharing → copy the “Secret address in iCal format”.
calendar_links.how_outlook: Outlook: Settings → Calendar → Shared calendars → “Publish a calendar” → copy the ICS link.
calendar_links.confirm_remove: Remove “{name}”? The calendar and its events disappear from xenaxio.
calendar_links.paused: Paused after several failures. “Refresh” tries again.
calendar_links.events_failed: {count} events could not be taken over.
calendar_links.link_intro: With this secret link you see a xenaxio calendar in Google, Outlook or Apple Calendar. Anyone with the link can see the events – do not pass it on.
calendar_links.confirm_new_link: Create a new link? The current link stops working – also in Google or Outlook.
calendar_links.confirm_disable: Disable the link? Google, Outlook & co. will no longer get events.
calendar_links.add_google: Google Calendar: “Other calendars” on the left → “+” → “From URL” → paste the link.
calendar_links.add_outlook: Outlook: “Add calendar” → “Subscribe from web” → paste the link.
calendar_links.delay: Google refreshes subscribed calendars on its own, only about every 8–24 hours; Outlook every few hours. It cannot be made faster. There the calendar is for viewing only.
